item.text:
**1B.7 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

I searched directly with several query formulations and stopped after a short pass. The evidence is **mostly negative**: I found some continued institutional engagement with the IAEA, but much stronger signs of inspector resistance, hardline dominance, and nuclear-security decision-making inside loyalist/ideological channels rather than independent expert ones.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Iran will not impede IAEA access, head of its atomic organisation says` | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-12-14 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/) | AEOI head Mohammad Eslami said Iran would not obstruct UN nuclear-watchdog inspections and would operate within safeguards. This is the clearest 2024 sign of continued reliance on formal verification institutions. | `1B.7`, `1B.4`, `1B.3` |
| `Iran and IAEA will continue talks aimed at ending impasse, Grossi says` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-07 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaeas-grossi-seeks-deal-with-iran-on-nuclear-steps-soon-3425312) | After visiting Iran, IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said talks would continue and a package of measures should be reached soon. This shows the institutional channel was still active, but it is indirect evidence of Khamenei prioritizing expertise over loyalists. | `1B.7`, `1B.4` |
| `IAEA Board passes resolution against Iran on cooperation, inspectors` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-05 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-resolution-against-iran-on-cooperation-inspectors-3472087) | The IAEA Board called on Iran to reverse its barring of inspectors, and Reuters said Iran had removed many experienced inspectors. This is strong evidence against risk-reducing institutionalism and suggests a preference for tighter ideological/security control. | `1B.7`, `1B.3`, `1B.4` |
| `Iranian commander warns Tehran could review its 'nuclear doctrine' amid Israeli threats` | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-04-18 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/iranian-commander-warns-tehran-could-review-its-nuclear-doctrine/2046641/) | Ahmad Haghtalab, the commander in charge of nuclear security, said Israeli threats could push Tehran to review and deviate from its nuclear doctrine. That points to nuclear-security decisions being voiced by an IRGC commander, not insulated expert institutions. | `1B.7`, `1B.2`, `1B.3` |
| `Iran’s presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-25 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879) | Reuters said Khamenei ensured candidates sharing his hard-line views dominated the presidential contest and that the Guardian Council was a hard-line vetting body aligned to him. This is broader than nuclear policy, but it supports the reading that the decision environment was loyalist-heavy rather than expert-driven. | `1B.7`, `1B.6` |

**Assessment**

- The best positive evidence is **continued IAEA access/talks**, but that is narrower than real investment in independent expertise.
- The stronger evidence is **inspector resistance** and **hardline control of the political environment**, plus a nuclear-security commander publicly floating doctrine review.
- I found **no solid 2024 evidence** that Khamenei created new independent technical bodies, empowered non-ideological experts, or meaningfully displaced loyalists from nuclear/security decisions.

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find a 2024 source showing Khamenei explicitly elevating technocrats over ideologues on the nuclear file.
- I also did **not** find evidence of a new expert-led safety review or command-and-control reform package. The record is mostly institutional continuity at best, and hardline control at worst.
